itens.texto:
Hi Mustafa,

We confirm all four changes from 1 January 2027:

- Contribution wage floor/ceiling: EGP 3,200 / 19,300 per month (from 2,700 / 16,700). Executive Regulations (PM Decree 2437/2021), Art. 53: both limits rise by 15% every 1 January for seven years (2021–2027), rounded up to the nearest EGP 100 (2,700 × 1.15 → 3,200; 16,700 × 1.15 → 19,300). NOSI's 2027 notice is not yet published.
- Rates: employee 11% → 11.5%, employer 18.75% → 19.25%. Law 148/2019, Art. 19 (last paragraph): the contribution rate increases by 1% every seven years from 1 January 2020, split equally between employer and employee; Executive Regulations, Art. 57 applies it to the old-age, disability and death branch (9% → 9.5%; 12% → 12.5%).

EG-CCG-001 updated to v1.5 with the 2027 values: [link]

@mjain For Reg. 23 (EG Social Security), from 01-01-2027: floor/ceiling 38,400 / 231,600 per year in all bands; under-60 base band employee 10% → 10.5% and employer 14.75% → 15.25%. We expect the 1%/4% layer and the 60+ band to stay unchanged, as they do not include the old-age branch; please confirm against the band composition. Would you like us to raise a Regulation Update task, or will you handle it from here?

Best regards,

pedido: SDL só sobre componentes CPF-able está certo?
Atualizar o 62866 como CPF-able no WTC?
itens.texto:
Hi @nharmy,

Yes, SDL follows the CPF definition of wages: both Acts define "wages" in the same terms ("remuneration in money, including any bonus, due or granted to a person in respect of the person's employment", SDL Act 1979 s.2; CPF Act 1953 s.2). A childbirth allowance paid in cash through payroll is therefore wages for both CPF and SDL; only gifts in kind on the birth of a child are excluded (CPF Board, "Which allowances and payments attract CPF contributions", Staff welfare benefits).

WTC V4.3 sets 62866 as subject to CPF, as Additional Wages: it is a one-off payment, not remuneration "wholly or exclusively in respect of employment during that month" (CPF Act, First Schedule para 5(d)–(e)). A fixed amount paid for each month's work is Ordinary Wages and should use a recurring OW code rather than 62866.

pedido: Payroll ou fora? o que a Mercans precisa
itens.texto:
Hi @anaik,

For an employer-paid childcare subsidy paid once a year through payroll:

1. Tax: taxable. Salary income includes "各種補助費" (all kinds of subsidies) (Income Tax Act art. 14(1), Category 3), and no art. 4 exemption applies; the exemption for childcare subsidies covers only those paid by the government (MOF ruling 台財稅字第09700315650號). As non-monthly salary, 5% is withheld when the payment reaches NT$90,501 (2026 threshold); below that there is no withholding (Withholding Regulations for Salary Income arts. 6–7; MOF tax portal Q&A 1506). Either way it is reported in the annual withholding / non-withholding statement (Income Tax Act arts. 89(3) and 92).

2. Statutory insurance: LI, EI, Labour Pension and the NHI insured amount follow "wages" under Labor Standards Act art. 2(3) (LI Act art. 14 and Enforcement Rules art. 27; EI Act art. 40; Labor Pension Act art. 3; NHI Enforcement Rules art. 46). A discretionary, non-recurring welfare payment is not counted (LSA Enforcement Rules art. 10; CLA Order 勞保2字第0950114071號), so it does not change the insured salary bracket. If it becomes a fixed or contractual entitlement, it becomes wages.

3. Once-a-year payment: no NHI employee supplementary premium, as subsidies are not incentive bonuses (Supplementary Premium Regulations art. 3(1)(1); NHIA guide v115.1). The employer supplementary premium (2.11%) applies in the month paid (NHI Act art. 34).

4. Payroll: processing it through payroll as a separate one-off earning gives the correct withholding and annual reporting. The "refund application" is the employer's own claim for the Ministry of Labor childcare subsidy (育兒補貼, up to NT$10,000 per employee per year), filed at childcare.mol.gov.tw.

Regards,

@mjain Spec review done against the MOF e-filing rules (綜合所得稅資料電子申報作業要點, Dec 2025 edition); spec v1.3 attached, changes in light blue.

**Verdict:** your 3 points are right, but none of them was in the spec yet. They are now in, along with the other gaps. Not ready for development until the open points below are answered.

**Changes**
1. Resident = YTD for the tax year, one file a year. Non-resident = one file **per payment date**, not per calendar month (file name, serial starting "00" and never repeated for the same UBN, field 31 = payment date, year = payment year). Resident serials start with "01" so they never collide with non-resident ones.
2. Field 9 is the **tax withheld**, not an exemption: renamed "Tax Withheld Amount" and mapped per column P (2552+2572+2582+2592 YTD; 2594 for format 93; 2593 non-resident). The old mapping 58100+58105 is why it was not coming.
3. Period: resident = hire month (or 01) to termination month (or 12); non-resident = YYYMMYYYMM of the month paid (year-month, not dates).
4. Field 5 now mapped: 93 for severance (62180:62182), 50 for the rest; an employee with both gets two records.
5. Also corrected: voluntary pension = 2517 (58105 does not exist); country code blank unless ID type 3/5/6/7/8/9/A; treaty code blank instead of "XX"; TIN "NOTIN" by ID type; name and address in a single width (full-width for Chinese text), address starting with the postcode; ID type list; text types for year/period/date fields; file format (UTF-8, "|", 32 fields) and file name.

**Questions**
1. Do we generate the full .U8 (with the declaration and payer records) or a CSV to import into IMX?
2. Are 62200:62209 already inside 58008 (double count)?
3. Which system fields/functions hold the payment date, hire/termination dates, Chinese name, country of residence, foreign TIN, treaty code, the non-resident serial counter and full-width conversion? Marked "TO BE CONFIRMED BY MOHIT/BA" in columns H/J.
4. Which tax account applies when format 93 (severance) is paid to a non-resident?
5. Should Pension (62640:62649) and Gratuity/EOS (62930) go to format 93 (retirement income) instead of 50?

@manjitbali could you share the current output after your January changes?
